hints: Each original tree edge must belong to a cycle after adding connections.
Every leaf needs at least one new incident edge.
Pair leaves from opposite halves of their DFS order.
analogy: A new connection between two leaves reinforces the entire tree path between them.
example: A star with four leaves needs two connections: pair the first leaf with the third and the second with the fourth.
algorithm: Root the tree at any non-leaf vertex and collect its L leaves in DFS order. Let h=ceil(L/2). Add edges between leaf i and leaf i+h for i from 0 to floor(L/2)-1. If L is odd, also connect leaf h-1 to leaf 0. Print the ceil(L/2) added edges.
correctness: Each new edge can cover at most two leaf endpoints, so at least ceil(L/2) edges are necessary. Leaves of any rooted subtree form a contiguous interval in DFS order. Pairing opposite halves ensures every proper such interval has a pair crossing its boundary; hence every original tree edge lies on a cycle and cannot disconnect the graph alone.
complexity: For n vertices, DFS and output take O(n) time and O(n) space.
